stages.name: Business growth
stages.title: Business growth
stages.sub: Why firms grow, and how organic and vertical growth differ.

steps.q: A bakery owner notices that a bigger bakery down the road earns far more profit each year, and could survive a bad month more easily than she could. What is pulling her towards expanding?
steps.right: Wanting more profit and more safety from being bigger
steps.wrong: Wanting to close the business down
steps.hint: Think about what a small firm gains by becoming a larger one.
steps.pre: Higher profit, spreading risk and gaining market power are all

steps.q: The bakery reinvests its own profits to open a second shop and hire more staff, rather than buying another bakery. Has it grown using its own resources, or by taking over someone else's business?
steps.right: Using its own resources and sales
steps.hint: Where did the money and the new shop come from: the firm itself, or an outside company it bought?

steps.q: Wheat is milled into flour, the flour is baked into bread, and the bread is sold in a shop. Are milling, baking and selling all the same point in this process, or different points along it?
steps.wrong: All the same point in the process
steps.hint: Does flour become bread at the same moment it is sold to a customer, or earlier?

steps.q: Instead of growing its own shops, the bakery buys the flour mill that supplies its wheat, and also buys a chain of cafés that sell its bread to customers. Is it growing within its own stage of production, or joining together different stages of the same supply chain?
steps.right: Joining together different stages of the same supply chain
steps.wrong: Growing within its own single stage only
steps.hint: Flour milling and running cafés are different stages from baking bread. Is the bakery staying at one stage or spreading across stages?

steps.q: The bakery buys the café chain that sells its bread to customers. Is that café chain a stage closer to the final customer, or a stage further back towards raw materials?
steps.right: A stage closer to the final customer
steps.wrong: A stage further back towards raw materials

steps.right: A stage further back towards raw materials
steps.wrong: A stage closer to the final customer
steps.hint: The mill supplies an ingredient before baking even starts. Is that nearer the raw material end or the customer end?
